text:
maria: heads up — we started getting a surge of 429s for multiple customers around 09:12 PDT. Support is getting noisy. looks like rate limiter kicked in hard.
jake: saw that. which limiter? global or per-tenant?
alice: logs show 'quota_exhausted' with scope=global for a bunch of orgs. odd — we should be per-tenant by default.
maria: exactly. initial hypothesis: a config change rolled that accidentally turned per-tenant enforcement off.
ops-deploy-bot: deploy by @nate merged: feat(limiter): add dynamic burst config (commit: a3f7c9b) — deployed at 09:05 PDT
nate: I pushed the dynamic burst PR this morning. I tested locally but maybe the default fallback is wrong in prod.
support-bot: Tickets created: S-11243, S-11244 — customers reporting 429s and increased latency. reported start 09:10-09:15 PDT
jake: grabbing recent logs — copying snip:
```
[09:12:08] limiter: quota_exhausted scope=global bucket=api_write org_id=org-123 req_id=abcd
[09:12:09] limiter: quota_exhausted scope=global bucket=api_write org_id=org-456 req_id=efgh
[09:12:09] limiter: deny reason=burst_disabled config_version=2026-03-15T08:59
```
maria: that config_version is the deploy you mentioned ops-deploy-bot — nates PR
nate: posting the config change I merged (redacted):
```
-rate_limiter:
-  enforcement: per_tenant
-  max_per_tenant: 100
-  global_cap: 10000
+rate_limiter:
+  enforcement: global
+  global_cap: 10000
+  dynamic_burst: true
```
alice: oh wow — enforcement flipped to global. that explains aggregation into one pool.
jake: production validation should have prevented a switch from per_tenant -> global without a guard. we have a safety check in the YAML validator but not for this combo.
maria: mitigation plan — immediate steps?
nate: we can roll back the deploy to previous commit. can do immediate rollback to a3f7c9b-1
ops-deploy-bot: rollback requested by @nate for commit a3f7c9b — started
alice: while rollback happens, can we enforce an emergency per-tenant cap via a runtime flag? i can push a hotfix to the limiter service to treat global enforcement as a no-op and apply per-tenant caps if runtime ENV ENABLE_PER_TENANT_SAFE=true
jake: that's safer than waiting for full rollback. do the hotfix and flip the runtime flag.
alice: pushing hotfix now — will instrument with extra logging.
maria: also add temporary rules at the API gateway: max requests per org = 120/s. support can contact high-volume customers to throttle client-side.
support-bot: Noted. Messaging drafted for customers: "We're applying temporary safeguards to stabilize request throttling — ETA resolution 30 min."
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: LIM-2026-03-15-01 — rate-limiter misconfiguration causing global quota exhaustion. severity=P2
nate: rollback complete at 09:28 PDT. looking at metrics — 429 rate down 78% but still some residual errors due to burst backlog.
jake: gateway caps are active. reducing token refill aggressiveness might help; I'll nudge refill_rate from 50 -> 20 until traffic normalizes.
maria: quick postmortem notes here so we don't lose them:
- root cause: config change merged that set enforcement: global (intended feature was dynamic burst but default guard missing)
- impact: multiple customers received 429s; some high-throughput tenants starved other tenants
- detection: customer tickets + spike in quota_exhausted logs; automated alert didn’t fire because alert watches per-tenant error rate only
- mitigation: rollback + runtime safe-mode + gateway per-org caps + throttle tuning
- immediate action items: add config validation preventing enforcement flips without explicit force flag; add canary rollout for limiter config; augment alerts for global quota exhaustion; postmortem doc + customer outreach
nate: I'll own the rollback verification and write the postmortem draft. ETA 4 hours.
ajake: I'll own alerting changes and add a global quota exhaustion alert. ETA 2 days.
alice: I'll land the config validator and add unit tests. PR in-flight.
maria: support will send personalized updates for top 5 affected customers. ops to coordinate refunds/credits if needed.
support-bot: customer S-11243 asked for repro steps. example they sent:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Org-ID: org-123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
jake: repro locally — if you set RATE_LIMIT_ENFORCEMENT=global you can reproduce quickly by spawning many org headers in parallel.
alice: longer term: we should have a config schema change gating system and a UI preview for dynamic_burst toggles.
maria: agree. also add an automatic rollback if 429s spike after a config rollout within first 10 minutes.
nate: lesson learned — feature flags are great until they change default semantics. I take it.
maria: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for postmortem comments and final customer messaging. :thumbsup:
alice: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/limiter/pulls/472 (validator) — requesting review
jake: creating alert ticket: INC-4056
ops-deploy-bot: deploy finished: rollback commit a3f7c9b-1 at 09:28 PDT
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: LIM-2026-03-15-01 — mitigated (rollback + gateway caps) — next: postmortem
nate: will post the draft and owners in #postmortems when ready.
support-bot: top-5 customers notified at 09:45 PDT. awaiting replies.
maria: closing day note: include in weekly ops review. good job triaging fast."
